title: Tic-Tac-Toe
summary: Model an N by N tic-tac-toe game so that a Game coordinates turns and results while a Board owns the grid, and every move is checked in constant time.

tests.explain: X fills the whole top row on the fifth move. O only has two cells of its own, so the game ends with X_WINS and winner() reports X.

O tries an occupied cell and two cells off the board: all INVALID_MOVE, and none of them uses up O's turn. The attempt by X in the middle is NOT_YOUR_TURN because O still has to move, and then O's real move goes through.
X always moves first, so O's attempt is NOT_YOUR_TURN and nothing is placed. X then moves, and cannot move twice in a row.
O completes the middle column on the sixth move. After that, every move is GAME_OVER, whoever plays and wherever, and the winner does not change.
The main diagonal (0,0), (1,1), (2,2) belongs to X.
The anti-diagonal (0,2), (1,1), (2,0) belongs to X. A move after the end is GAME_OVER even when the cell is taken.
Nine moves fill the board and nobody has a line, so the ninth move returns DRAW and winner() is DRAW. Final board: X O X / X O O / O X X.
The ninth move fills the board and also completes the main diagonal. A win takes priority over a draw.
On a 4x4 board three in a row is not enough: both players reach three and the game goes on. X wins with the fourth cell of the top row.
O wins the 4x4 main diagonal on its fourth mark. X has three of the top row but never the fourth cell.
On a 1x1 board the first move fills a row, a column and both diagonals.
A 500x500 board: X plays the main diagonal while O plays the cells just above it. The win must be found on X's 500th move. Checking one move should cost O(1), not a scan of the board.

hints: Ask who owns what. The grid and its lines are one responsibility, turns and the end of the game are another. Which class should know that a row is complete?
A line is won when all n of its cells hold the same mark. Instead of scanning, keep one running total per row, per column and for each diagonal: +1 for an X, -1 for an O.
In move, check in this order: game already over, wrong player, bad or taken cell. Only after all three pass do you place the mark, update the four totals that cell touches, and look for |total| == n.

complexity.time: O(1) per move, O(n^2) to build or print the board
complexity.space: O(n^2) for the grid, O(n) for the line totals
